# Locality Guide: Funchal, Madeira, Portugal (1860–1900)

## Jurisdiction overview
- **Formed:** Funchal city chartered ca. 1508; the Distrito de Funchal (covering all of Madeira) dates from 1420, restructured as "Madeira" region in 1976.
- **Administrative center:** Funchal (island capital)
- **Parent jurisdiction:** Portugal; diocesan authority under the Diocese of Funchal (Bispado do Funchal), established 1514.
- **Economy:** Sugar, wine (Madeira wine), embroidery, fishing. Significant emigration to Brazil and Hawaii during this period.
- **Religious denominations:** Overwhelmingly Roman Catholic; small Anglican/Protestant community (British residents).
- **Key historical events:** Major emigration waves to Brazil, Hawaii (1878–1911), and the US.

## Boundary changes
- No significant boundary changes affecting record jurisdiction within 1860–1900. All of Madeira comprised the *Distrito de Funchal* under historical standardPlace "Funchal, Portugal" (+1420/+1976). After 1976 renamed "Madeira, Portugal."
- Records created before 1976 are filed under the historical jurisdiction; both standardPlace forms retrieve the same records on FamilySearch.

## Available record types

### Vital records (civil registration)
- **Start date:** Portuguese civil registration commenced nationally in 1878 (Código de Registo Civil).
- **Where held:** Madeira Regional Archive (abm.madeira.gov.pt) holds originals. FamilySearch collection 4426199 covers Madeira records.
- **Pre-registration alternatives:** Catholic parish registers are the primary source before 1878 and remain important through the 1880s–1890s.

### Church records
- **Primary FamilySearch collection:** "Portugal, Madeira, Catholic Church Records, 1044-1990" (collection 4426199) — 1,329,527 indexed records, 17,724,331 person profiles, 604,364 images.
- **Confirmed digitized parishes (1860–1900):** Santo António (baptisms + deaths 1860-1899, 85-99% indexed); São Gonçalo (baptisms 1870-1890, 81-96% indexed); São Pedro (deaths 1860-1874 confirmed). Additional parishes on further volume_search pages.
- **Language:** Portuguese (some Latin in older registers).
- **Access:** Name-searchable on FamilySearch (coll. 4426199); also indexed on FindMyPast and MyHeritage.

### Census records
- Portuguese national censuses: 1864, 1878, 1890, 1900. Not indexed online; held at ANTT and ABM.
- Róis de Confessados (annual parish household lists) available via ANTT — useful census substitute.

### Probate and court records
- Held at Madeira Regional Archive and ANTT; not systematically digitized for FamilySearch.

### Passport records
- "Portugal, Madeira Passports 1872-1910" on Ancestry and at abm.madeira.gov.pt/pesquisa/passaportes/.
- FamilySearch volume for Funchal passport applications 1859–1863 (0% name-indexed, full-text searchable only).

## Repository guide

### Online repositories
| Repository | Collections | Access |
|---|---|---|
| FamilySearch | Portugal, Madeira Catholic Church Records 1044-1990 (4426199); national Baptisms/Marriages/Deaths indexes | Free |
| Tombo.pt | tombo.pt/en/d/madeira — Madeira civil reg, church records, passports | Free |
| Ancestry | Portugal Select Baptisms/Marriages/Deaths; Madeira Passports 1872-1910 | Subscription |
| FindMyPast | Portugal Baptism/Marriage/Death Indexes 1570-1910 | Subscription |
| Madeira Regional Archive | abm.madeira.gov.pt — online passport search and catalog | Free |

## Records NOT online
- Portuguese national census records (1864, 1878, 1890, 1900) — held at ANTT and ABM.
- Róis de Confessados — partial via ANTT; not indexed on FamilySearch.
- Notarial records (escrituras, testamentos) — physical at ABM.

## Research tips
- Identify the correct parish first; search national Madeira collection (4426199) by name, then drill into parish volumes.
- 'de Jesus' is a very common Marian surname for women in 19th-century Madeira — distinguish by parents' names, age, and parish.
- After 1878, search both parish and civil registers.
- Baptism records name both parents — the key evidence for identifying a child's mother.
- Tombo.pt and the ABM online catalog are important cross-checks alongside FamilySearch.

entry.rationale: Collection 4426199 (Portugal, Madeira, Catholic Church Records, 1044-1990) is the primary repository for all Funchal parish marriage registers: 1.3M indexed records, 17.7M person profiles, 604K images. Searching for Antonio Fernandes Lucas as groom should surface every recorded marriage across all Funchal parishes. Portuguese Catholic marriage registers name both parties, their parents, witnesses, and date. The 1860-1895 window covers any pre-1890 marriage to Antonia de Jesus and the ca. 1890 marriage to Maria Joana for cross-verification. Locality guide loc_001 confirms this collection is searchable by name (85-99% indexed in most parish volumes).

Collection 1520605 (Portugal Marriages, 1670-1910) is a national index (45,182 records) that may surface records not captured in the Madeira-specific collection, or confirm a find from item 1 with a second indexed entry. Fallback if item 1 yields no marriage to Antonia de Jesus, or used to verify any positive hit. Searching on FamilySearch is free and fast.

Catholic baptism registers in Madeira name the child's father AND mother in every entry. Searching collection 4426199 for Antonio Fernandes Lucas as father across all Funchal parishes 1860-1900 will reveal which women bore children with him and when: if Antonia de Jesus appears as mother in baptisms before ca. 1890 and Maria Joana appears after, this constitutes strong indirect evidence of two distinct relationships. Godparent names in these same records often identify close relatives and FAN-cluster associates who may appear in other record types. Covers both q_001 (Antonia de Jesus as wife) and the related daughter-Maria question. Santo António, São Gonçalo, and São Pedro parish volumes 1860-1899 are confirmed digitized and 85-99% name-indexed per loc_001 volume survey.

Several Santo António batismos volumes from 1860-1869 are confirmed 0% name-indexed and not reachable by record_search (loc_001). A full-text co-occurrence search via the search-full-text skill — searching 'Lucas' + 'Antonia' (or 'Fernandes' + 'Antonia') across the unindexed Madeira corpus — will surface any page where both terms appear together, including marriage banns, baptism entries, and burial records that indexed search cannot reach. This is particularly important for the 1860-1878 pre-civil-registration window. Route this item to the search-full-text skill, not record_search.

Portuguese civil registration began in 1878. Collection 4474701 (Portugal, Civil Records, 1437-2023) covers civil marriage registers post-1878. The ca. 1890 marriage to Maria Joana should appear here if conducted civilly. Searching Antonio Fernandes Lucas in civil marriage records verifies the tree-recorded Maria Joana marriage and may surface an earlier or additional civil marriage to Antonia de Jesus (possible if any marriage occurred after 1878). Civil marriage records name both parties and their parents, supplying full identification. This also independently verifies or challenges the 'ca. 1890' date in the tree, which is currently unsourced.

Tombo.pt (tombo.pt/en/d/madeira) and the Madeira Regional Archive online catalog (biblioteca.abm.madeira.gov.pt) provide access to Madeira civil and church records not indexed on FamilySearch, and support name-based searching. Searching Antonio Fernandes Lucas at these portals cross-checks FamilySearch findings and may surface additional marriage or baptism records, particularly for post-1878 civil records where FamilySearch coverage of Madeira may be incomplete. Route to search-external-sites skill.

## Did Antonio Fernandes Lucas (GK89-82B) marry Antonia de Jesus?

**Conclusion: No.** GK89-82B’s only documented marriage is to Maria Joana on 8 February 1890 in Santo António, Funchal. No record connects him to any woman named Antonia de Jesus.

### Evidence

**Two independent records confirm the 1890 marriage to Maria Joana.** The Catholic church record (6BG7-FC2X, src_001) and the civil registration (X91Y-HHF4, src_002) were created on the same date by different registrars — the parish priest and the civil registrar — and constitute independent evidentiary units on the same event. Both name the same groom (Antonio Fernandes Lucas, father José), the same bride (Maria Joana / Maria Joanna de Jesus, parents Antonio de Nóbrega + Luiza de Jesus), and the same date and place (8 Feb 1890, Santo António, Funchal). The church-record groom persona was scored against GK89-82B by `same_person` and returned 0.895 — a strong match. The civil record’s suspect bride name ‘Antonio de Jesus’ (gender=Female in the index) is a transcription error: five corroborating attributes (parents, birthplace, birth year, marriage date, dual registration) confirm this is the same Maria Joana.

**The 1859 ‘Antonia de Jesus’ marriage belongs to a different man.** Record 6BG7-MQ3D (src_003) shows a groom also named Antonio Fernandes Lucas marrying Antonia de Jesus on 20 July 1859 in Santo António. However, that groom’s father is **Manoel** Fernandes Lucas (a_054, a_056), whereas GK89-82B’s father is **José** Fernandes Lucas — established independently by the 1890 church marriage (a_005) and the 1890 civil registration (a_029). In 19th-century Madeiran naming practice, ‘Fernandes Lucas’ is the paternal surname inherited from the father. Two different fathers name two different branches of the Lucas family: this groom (I3, the namesake) is from the Manoel branch; GK89-82B is from the José branch.

**The 1890 baptism corroborates the Manoel branch.** Record 6NGD-3SZ7 (src_004) baptizes a child born 18 July 1890 whose father is ‘Antonio Fernandes Lucas’ and mother is ‘Antonia de Jesus Fernandes Lucas.’ The child’s maternal grandparents are named as **Manoel Fernandes Lucas** and Luiza de Jesus (a_080, a_084) — the same parents as the 1859 namesake groom (I3). This establishes that the ‘Antonia de Jesus Fernandes Lucas’ in the 1890 baptism is I3’s wife and daughter of the Manoel branch. She is not a spouse of GK89-82B.

**No affirmative evidence exists** for a marriage or relationship between GK89-82B and any woman named Antonia de Jesus at any date.

### Conflict resolved

A minor conflict in GK89-82B’s birth year (tree: 1838 from christening vs. marriage records: 1839 approximate self-report) was evaluated and resolved in favour of the christening date as the contemporaneous primary source (c_001). The discrepancy is within normal rounding error and does not affect the marriage question.

### GPS assessment

The conclusion rests on direct evidence (two positive marriage records establishing the only marriage) and negative evidence (the 1859 and 1890 records document a different family branch). The two positive records are independent. The negative evidence is cross-corroborated across two records from different years naming the same Manoel branch. Conflicts have been addressed. The search was reasonably exhaustive for the specific question as framed.

## Did Antonio Fernandes Lucas (GK89-82B) marry Antonia de Jesus?

**Conclusion: No.** Antonio Fernandes Lucas (GK89-82B, b. 22 Apr 1838, Santo António, Funchal, Madeira) has one documented marriage: to Maria Joana on 8 February 1890 in Santo António, Funchal. No record connects him to any woman named Antonia de Jesus.

### GPS Element 1 — Reasonably Exhaustive Research

Two FamilySearch collections covering Madeiran records for the target period were searched with multiple query variants (pli_001 and pli_005 for marriages; pli_003 for baptisms as father). Nine log entries document the search process. Four records bearing on the question were extracted. Planned full-text and external searches (pli_004, pli_006) were skipped because the recovered evidence base is sufficient without ambiguity and further indexed searching is not expected to yield new material evidence.

### GPS Element 2 — Evidence Analysis

**Evidence affirming the 1890 marriage:** Two independent sources confirm GK89-82B’s sole marriage:
- *Catholic church record 6BG7-FC2X (src_001):* Groom Antonio Fernandes Lucas, father José Fernandes Lucas, mother Francisca Luisa da Conceicao, marries Maria Joanna de Jesus (b. 1869, parents Antonio de Nóbrega + Luisa de Jesus) on 8 Feb 1890, Santo António. `same_person` match score vs. GK89-82B: 0.895 (strong). *Source classification: original/primary/direct.*
- *Civil registration X91Y-HHF4 (src_002):* Same groom, same parents, same date, same place. Bride indexed as ‘Antonio de Jesus’ (gender=Female); suspect transcription — five independent attributes (parents, birthplace, birth year, marriage date, dual same-day registration) identify her as the same Maria Joana from src_001. *Source classification: original/primary/direct.*

These two records were created by different registrars (parish priest; civil registrar) and constitute independent evidentiary units. They agree on every material fact.

**Evidence excluding an Antonia de Jesus connection:**
- *Catholic church record 6BG7-MQ3D (src_003):* A groom also named ‘Antonio Fernandes Lucas’ married ‘Antonia de Jesus’ on 20 July 1859 in Santo António. This groom’s father is named **Manoel** Fernandes Lucas (a_054, a_056). GK89-82B’s father is **José** Fernandes Lucas (established independently by a_005 and a_029). In 19th-century Madeiran naming practice the paternal surname ‘Fernandes Lucas’ was transmitted from the father; two different fathers name two different lines of descent. The 1859 groom (I3) is from the Manoel branch; GK89-82B is from the José branch. *Source classification: original/primary/direct. Evidence type: negative.*
- *Baptismal record 6NGD-3SZ7 (src_004):* A child baptized 31 August 1890 in Santo António has father ‘Antonio Fernandes Lucas’ and mother ‘Antonia de Jesus Fernandes Lucas.’ The child’s maternal grandparents are **Manoel** Fernandes Lucas + Luiza de Jesus (a_080, a_084) — the same parents as the 1859 namesake groom (I3). This places the ‘Antonia de Jesus Fernandes Lucas’ in the 1890 baptism as I3’s wife, a daughter of the Manoel branch. The assertion a_094 explicitly documents this negative finding. *Source classification: original/primary/direct. Evidence type: negative.*

### GPS Element 3 — Correlation and Analysis

The father-name conflict between the 1859 marriage record and GK89-82B’s established parentage is independently corroborated by the 1890 baptismal record’s naming of Manoel Fernandes Lucas as maternal grandfather. Two records from different years, different event types, and different registrations converge on the same family structure for the Manoel branch. This cross-corroboration rules out the alternative explanation (a single misrecorded father name in one record) and confirms that the Lucas family in Santo António had two distinct branches bearing the surname.

A minor birth-year conflict (GK89-82B tree: 1838 vs. marriage records: approximate 1839) was resolved in favour of the contemporaneous christening record (c_001). This conflict has no bearing on the marriage question.

### GPS Element 4 — Soundly Reasoned, Written Conclusion

The preponderance of direct and negative evidence leads to a single defensible conclusion: Antonio Fernandes Lucas (GK89-82B) never married Antonia de Jesus. His only documented marriage is to Maria Joana, 8 February 1890. The appearance of an ‘Antonia de Jesus’ wife in records from Santo António is explained by a collateral branch of the Lucas family — the descendants of Manoel Fernandes Lucas — not by any connection to GK89-82B.

## Did Antonio Fernandes Lucas (GK89-82B) marry Antonia de Jesus?

**Conclusion: Probably not.** Antonio Fernandes Lucas (GK89-82B, b. 22 Apr 1838, Santo António, Funchal, Madeira) has one documented marriage: to Maria Joana on 8 February 1890 in Santo António, Funchal. No record connects him to any woman named Antonia de Jesus. One open identity thread prevents a 'proved' tier (see h_001).

### GPS Element 1 — Reasonably Exhaustive Research

Two FamilySearch collections covering Madeiran records for the target period were searched with multiple query variants (pli_001 and pli_005 for marriages; pli_003 for baptisms as father). Nine log entries document the search process. Four records bearing on the question were extracted. Planned full-text (pli_004) and external searches (pli_006) were skipped as current evidence is sufficient to reach a probable negative conclusion; executing them could upgrade the tier to 'proved.' The original image for 6NGD-3SZ7 (ark:/61903/1:2:H92K-X1N6) has not been read — doing so is the primary path to resolving h_001.

### GPS Element 2 — Evidence Analysis

**Two independent records confirm GK89-82B's sole marriage:**
- *Catholic church record 6BG7-FC2X (src_001):* Groom Antonio Fernandes Lucas, father José Fernandes Lucas, mother Francisca Luisa da Conceicao, marries Maria Joanna de Jesus (b. 1869, parents Antonio de Nóbrega + Luisa de Jesus) on 8 Feb 1890, Santo António. `same_person` score vs. GK89-82B: 0.895 (strong). *Original/primary/direct.*
- *Civil registration X91Y-HHF4 (src_002):* Same groom, same parents, same date and place. Bride indexed as 'Antonio de Jesus' (gender=Female); five corroborating attributes identify her as the same Maria Joana from src_001. *Original/primary/direct.*

These records were created by different registrars and constitute independent evidentiary units that agree on every material fact.

**Negative evidence points away from an Antonia de Jesus connection:**
- *Catholic church record 6BG7-MQ3D (src_003):* A namesake groom (I3) married Antonia de Jesus (I6) on 20 July 1859. His father is **Manoel** Fernandes Lucas (a_054), not GK89-82B's father **José** (a_005, a_029). Two different fathers = two different men. *Original/primary/direct. Evidence type: negative.*
- *Baptismal record 6NGD-3SZ7 (src_004):* A child born 18 July 1890 has mother 'Antonia de Jesus Fernandes Lucas' (I9), whose maternal grandparents are Manoel Fernandes Lucas + Luiza de Jesus (a_080, a_084) — the Manoel-branch parents. This places I9 firmly in the Manoel branch. The father in this record (I8) is also named 'Antonio Fernandes Lucas'; his own parentage has not been independently confirmed (see h_001 and a_087). *Original/primary/direct. Evidence type: negative (for I9's branch), indeterminate (for I8's identity).*

### Open Thread — h_001

The 1890 baptism uses the mother's (I9's) Manoel-branch parentage to link the 'Antonia de Jesus Fernandes Lucas' in that record to the collateral family. However, the identity of the FATHER (I8, also 'Antonio Fernandes Lucas') is not directly confirmed as belonging to the Manoel branch rather than to GK89-82B's José branch. The paternal-grandfather entry in the index (a_087) appeared from an adjacent register entry and was flagged for original-image confirmation. This open thread, combined with a_094's own acknowledgement that 'a separate Antonia de Jesus from José's branch may exist but has not been found,' prevents escalation to 'proved.' Hypothesis h_001 documents the specific question.

**Upgrade path:** Read the original register image (ark:/61903/1:2:H92K-X1N6) to confirm the paternal_grandfather's name. If the grandfather is Manoel Fernandes Lucas (= I4), h_001 can be confirmed and ps_001 upgraded to 'proved.'

### GPS Element 3 — Correlation and Analysis

The father-name conflict between the 1859 marriage record and GK89-82B's established parentage is independently corroborated by the 1890 baptismal record's maternal-grandparent naming. Two records from different years, different event types, and different registrations converge on the Manoel branch for the 'Antonia de Jesus' connection. A birth-year conflict (tree: 1838 vs. marriage records: approximate 1839) was resolved in favour of the christening record as the contemporaneous primary source (c_001). This conflict has no bearing on the marriage question.

### GPS Element 4 — Soundly Reasoned, Written Conclusion

The preponderance of direct and negative evidence supports the conclusion that Antonio Fernandes Lucas (GK89-82B) never married Antonia de Jesus. His only documented marriage is to Maria Joana, 8 February 1890. The appearance of an 'Antonia de Jesus' connection in Santo António records is explained by the collateral Manoel-branch Lucas family. One image review (h_001) is required to upgrade from probable to proved.

entry.informant_bias_notes: Negative-evidence synthesis: the death record's mother name (Antonia de Jesus) is the key discriminator. entry.narrative_markdown:
## Q_002: Did GK89-82B have a daughter named Maria who died young?

### Conclusion: Probably not.

Three independent search vectors — Catholic church baptisms, Catholic church deaths, and civil deaths — all returned the same finding: every candidate 'Maria Fernandes Lucas' who died young in Santo António, Funchal is a child of the **Manoel branch** of the family, not of GK89-82B.

### Evidence

**1. Baptism of Maria Fernandes Lucas, 11 Oct 1886 (6NG6-XHM2, src_006):**
The register entries for this Maria name her father as Antonio Fernandes Lucas and record her paternal grandfather as **Manuel Fernandes Lucas** (with paternal grandmother Luiza de Jesus). GK89-82B's documented father was **José** Fernandes Lucas — not Manuel. This is the single most diagnostic piece of evidence: the grandfather's name places this child unambiguously in the Manoel branch, not GK89-82B's family.

**2. Catholic church death of Maria Fernandes Lucas, 30 May 1889 (6B2L-FKDG, src_005):**
The death register names father Antonio Fernandes Lucas and mother **Antonia de Jesus**. GK89-82B's only documented wife is **Maria Joana de Jesus** (married 8 Feb 1890). 'Antonia de Jesus' is the wife of the Manoel-branch Antonio Fernandes Lucas — a different woman from a different family branch. The discrepancy in the mother's name directly excludes GK89-82B from this child's parentage.

**3. Civil registration death of Maria Fernandes Lucas, 30 May 1889 (6YPM-36RZ):**
The civil registration death record independently corroborates record 2: same child, same date, same father Antonio Fernandes Lucas, same mother Antonia de Jesus. Two independent register types (church and civil) both name Antonia de Jesus — the consistency across independent sources strengthens the attribution to the Manoel branch.

**4. Timeline consideration:**
Maria was born in September 1886 and died in May 1889. GK89-82B married Maria Joana de Jesus on 8 February 1890 — **nine months after this Maria died**. A child born and dying before GK89-82B's documented marriage cannot be a daughter of that union. If GK89-82B had an undocumented earlier relationship with a woman named Antonia de Jesus, that would explain the mother's name — but no record supports such a relationship, and all Antonia de Jesus associations in Santo António's indexed records belong to the Manoel branch.

### Negative evidence summary

A total of five candidate records for 'Maria Fernandes Lucas who died young in Santo António with father Antonio Fernandes Lucas' were examined across baptism and death registers (church and civil). All five show Antonia de Jesus as mother and/or Manuel Fernandes Lucas as paternal grandfather. None shows Maria Joana de Jesus as mother.

### Open threads

- Unindexed records: the exhaustive declaration covers indexed sources only. Records not yet transcribed into the FamilySearch name index could theoretically contain a daughter Maria of GK89-82B + Maria Joana. No positive evidence for this exists.
- h_001 (the identity of the 1890 baptism father, I8) remains an open hypothesis from the q_001 investigation. The present evidence strengthens the inference that I8 is the Manoel-branch Antonio Fernandes Lucas (father=Manuel, wife=Antonia de Jesus), further corroborating the Manoel-branch attribution of all 'Maria' records.

### GPS assessment

The conclusion rests on negative evidence from three independently sourced record types, corroborated by a timeline conflict (child predates the marriage). The conclusion is rated **probable** rather than proved because absence of positive evidence in indexed records does not preclude the existence of unindexed records. The preponderance of available evidence supports the conclusion that GK89-82B did not have a daughter named Maria who died young.

## Q_002: Did GK89-82B have a daughter named Maria who died young?

### Conclusion: Probably not.

Five independent records in three record types — Catholic church baptisms, Catholic church deaths, and civil death registration — all returned the same finding: every candidate 'Maria Fernandes Lucas' who died young in Santo António, Funchal is a child of the **Manoel branch** of the family, not of GK89-82B.

### Evidence

**1. Baptism of Maria Fernandes Lucas, 11 Oct 1886 (6NG6-XHM2, src_006 / a_111, a_116):**
The baptism register names the child's father as Antonio Fernandes Lucas and records her paternal grandfather as **Manuel Fernandes Lucas** (paternal grandmother: Luiza de Jesus). GK89-82B's documented father was **José** Fernandes Lucas — not Manuel. This is the single most diagnostic piece of evidence: the grandfather's name places this child unambiguously in the Manoel branch, entirely independently of the mother-name comparison.

**2. Catholic church death of Maria Fernandes Lucas, 30 May 1889 (6B2L-FKDG, src_005 / a_098, a_100):**
The death register names father Antonio Fernandes Lucas and mother **Antonia de Jesus**. GK89-82B's only documented wife is **Maria Joana de Jesus** (married 8 Feb 1890). 'Antonia de Jesus' is the wife of the Manoel-branch Antonio Fernandes Lucas — a different woman from a different family branch. The mother's name directly excludes GK89-82B from this child's parentage.

Note also the timeline: Maria was born in September 1886 and died in May 1889 — nine months *before* GK89-82B married Maria Joana on 8 February 1890. A child born and dying before GK89-82B's only documented marriage cannot be a daughter of that union.

**3. Civil registration death of Maria Fernandes Lucas, 30 May 1889 (6YPM-36RZ, src_007 / a_132, a_137):**
The civil registrar's record is independent of the Catholic church register (different authority, different officiant). It lists the same child, the same death date, and the same parents: father Antonio Fernandes Lucas, mother **Antonia de Jesus**. Two independent record sources — church and civil — converge on the same exclusion. This independence strengthens the attribution to the Manoel branch beyond what a single source could provide.

**4. Catholic church death of Maria Lucas, 5 Sep 1894 (6BCT-KZMJ, src_008 / a_143, a_144):**
This record addresses the post-marriage window directly. Maria Lucas was born in 1893 — three years after GK89-82B's marriage to Maria Joana in February 1890. A daughter born during the GK89-82B–Maria Joana marriage would fall exactly into this period. Yet the death register names this child's mother as **Antonia de Jesus** — not Maria Joana. Born in 1893, dying 5 September 1894, in Santo António: this is a second Manoel-branch daughter named Maria, showing that the pattern extends into the post-1890 period. No record with mother=Maria Joana de Jesus and daughter=Maria was found in any searched collection, even in the years after their marriage.

**5. Baptism of Maria Fernandes Lucas, 26 Dec 1892 (6NR2-ZMW7, src_009 / a_158, a_160):**
This record reveals the depth of the Manoel-branch family network in Santo António. The 1892 Maria's father is Antonio Fernandes Lucas (a Manoel-branch son), and her mother is **d'Antonia de Jesus Fernandes Lucas** — a woman who is herself a daughter of the Manoel-branch couple (Antonio Fernandes Lucas + Antonia de Jesus = I8 + I6). The name 'Antonia de Jesus' thus appears not only as a wife but as a maternal grandmother, and the inherited surname 'Fernandes Lucas' on the mother confirms her branch membership without ambiguity. This third-generation record demonstrates that all reachable 'Antonio Fernandes Lucas + daughter Maria' baptisms in Santo António trace through the Manoel-branch family network.

### Evidence synthesis

Five candidate records were examined across baptism and death registers (church and civil). The records span 1886–1894 and include both the pre-marriage and post-marriage periods relative to GK89-82B's February 1890 union with Maria Joana. All five records identify either (a) Antonia de Jesus as the child's mother, (b) Manuel Fernandes Lucas as the child's paternal grandfather, or (c) Antonia de Jesus as the child's maternal grandmother. None names Maria Joana de Jesus as a mother. The three naming mechanisms are independent — no single analytical step connects all five records — and they converge on the same conclusion: the entire indexed population of 'Maria Fernandes Lucas died young in Santo António' belongs to the Manoel branch, not to GK89-82B.

### Open threads

- **Unindexed records**: the exhaustive declaration covers indexed sources only. Records not yet transcribed into the FamilySearch name index could theoretically contain a daughter Maria of GK89-82B + Maria Joana. No positive evidence for this exists.
- **h_001 (I8 identity)**: the identity of the Manoel-branch father (I8) as a distinct person from GK89-82B was not independently confirmed by image review. However, the q_002 conclusion does not depend on I8's identity: record 1 above (6NG6-XHM2, a_116) proves the Manoel-branch attribution through the grandfather's name alone, without reference to I8's individual identity.

### GPS assessment

The conclusion rests on three types of negative evidence — mother's name (four records), grandfather's name (one baptism), and an independent civil registration — spanning pre-marriage and post-marriage periods, from three separate record types, with person-evidence linking establishing that the named mothers and grandfathers are identified Manoel-branch persons (I6, I8, I4). The conclusion is rated **probable** rather than proved because absence of positive evidence in indexed records does not preclude the existence of unindexed records naming Maria Joana as the mother. The preponderance of available evidence supports the conclusion that GK89-82B did not have a daughter named Maria who died young.

# Locality Guide: Funchal, Madeira, Portugal (1860–1900)

## Jurisdiction overview
- **Formed:** Funchal city chartered ca. 1508; the Distrito de Funchal (regional administrative unit covering all of Madeira) dates from 1420, restructured as "Madeira" region in 1976.
- **Administrative center:** Funchal (also the island's capital)
- **Parent jurisdiction:** Portugal (continental); diocesan authority under the Diocese of Funchal (Bispado do Funchal), established 1514.
- **Population during period:** Population data service unavailable; Madeira's population in the 19th century was predominantly concentrated in Funchal and surrounding parishes, heavily rural and agricultural.
- **Economy:** Sugar, wine (Madeira wine), embroidery, fishing. Significant emigration to Brazil and Hawaii during this period.
- **Ethnic composition:** Predominantly Portuguese; small British mercantile community in Funchal.
- **Religious denominations:** Overwhelmingly Roman Catholic; small Anglican/Protestant community (British residents).
- **Key historical events:** Major emigration waves to Brazil, Hawaii (1878–1911), and the US. Madeira remained under Portuguese sovereignty throughout.

## Boundary changes
- Funchal has been the administrative center of Madeira since the 15th century. No significant boundary changes affecting record jurisdiction within the 1860–1900 target period. The entire island of Madeira comprised the *Distrito de Funchal* under the historical place name "Funchal, Portugal" (place standard +1420/+1976). After 1976 the region was renamed "Madeira, Portugal."
- **Research implication:** Records created before 1976 are filed under the historical jurisdiction "Funchal, Portugal" or individual parish/civil registry offices within the district. Both standardPlace forms retrieve the same records on FamilySearch.

## Available record types

### Vital records (civil registration)
- **Start date:** Portuguese civil registration commenced nationally in 1878 (Código de Registo Civil). FamilySearch collection "Portugal, Civil Records, 1437–2023" (collection 4474701) covers civil registration.
- **What exists:** Births (nascimentos), marriages (casamentos), deaths (óbitos) from 1878 forward; however, the Madeira-specific civil records are most readily accessible through the Catholic Church Records collection which encompasses both ecclesiastical and later civil registrations.
- **Where held:** Madeira Regional Archive (Arquivo Regional da Madeira / abm.madeira.gov.pt) holds originals. FamilySearch has digitized them under collection 4426199.
- **Pre-registration alternatives:** Catholic parish registers (below) are the primary source for events before 1878 and remain the main source for events through the 1880s–1890s even after civil registration began, because the parish and civil registers often overlapped.

### Church records
- **Denomination:** Roman Catholic (Diocese of Funchal).
- **Record types:** Baptisms (batismos), marriages (casamentos), burials (óbitos/enterramentos), confirmations.
- **Primary FamilySearch collection:** **"Portugal, Madeira, Catholic Church Records, 1044-1990"** (collection ID 4426199) — 1,329,527 indexed records, 17,724,331 person profiles, 604,364 images. This is the most important collection for this research.
- **Supplementary national collections:** "Portugal Baptisms, 1570-1910" (1520601, 304,378 records); "Portugal Marriages, 1670-1910" (1520605, 45,182 records); "Portugal Deaths, 1640-1910" (1520606, 98,347 records).
- **Parishes digitized (confirmed by volume_search, 1860–1900 range):**
  - **Santo António, Funchal** — baptism volumes 1860–1899 (many volumes, 85–99% name-indexed, full-text searchable); burial/death volumes 1860–1899 (65–88% indexed, full-text searchable).
  - **São Gonçalo, Funchal** — baptism volumes 1870–1890 (81–96% indexed, full-text searchable).
  - **São Pedro, Funchal** — burial/death volumes 1860–1874 confirmed; likely continues beyond (further pages of volume_search not retrieved).
  - Additional parishes likely appear on subsequent pages of the volume search (13,859 total volumes were found).
- **Language:** Portuguese (Latin for some older registers).
- **Access:** Searchable by name on FamilySearch via collection 4426199; also indexed on FindMyPast ("Portugal Baptism Index, 1570-1910"; "Portugal Marriage Index, 1670-1910"; "Portugal Death Index, 1640-1910") and MyHeritage.

### Census records
- **Portuguese national census:** Portugal conducted national censuses in 1864, 1878, 1890, and 1900. These are not typically available on the major online genealogical databases in indexed form but may be held at the Arquivo Nacional Torre do Tombo (ANTT) and Madeira Regional Archive.
- **Ecclesiastical counts (Róis de Confessados):** Annual parish listings of parishioners who fulfilled Easter confession duties. These function as de-facto census substitutes. Available through ANTT (https://antt.dglab.gov.pt — Genealogia – Róis de Confessados das Paróquias). Coverage for Madeira parishes needs to be confirmed at ANTT.
- **Access:** Predominantly physical or via ANTT/Digitarq online portal; not systematically indexed on FamilySearch.

### Probate and court records
- **Types:** Wills (testamentos), estate inventories, court proceedings.
- **Where held:** Madeira Regional Archive; ANTT (digitarq.arquivos.pt for some). Also partially on tombo.pt.
- **Digitization:** FamilySearch has no Madeira-specific probate collection confirmed by tools. Tombo.pt lists "Portugal Probate Records" as a resource.

### Land records
- **Types:** Property registers, notarial acts, deeds (escrituras).
- **Where held:** Madeira Regional Archive; local notarial offices.
- **Access:** Not systematically digitized online; physical access at ABM.

### Military records
- **Relevant conflicts:** No major conflicts directly affecting Madeira 1860–1900, though Portuguese military conscription records exist.
- **Where held:** Arquivo Histórico Militar (ahm-germil.exercito.pt) holds Portuguese military records 1763–1908.
- **Access:** Partially online via AHM portal.

### Passport records
- **"Portugal, Madeira Passports 1872-1910"** — available on Ancestry (ancestry.com/search/collections/70774) and directly at the Madeira Regional Archive (abm.madeira.gov.pt/pesquisa/passaportes/).
- FamilySearch also has a volume for Funchal "Applications for Passport" 1859–1863 (image group 008038197_002, 832 images, 0% name-indexed, **full-text searchable only**).
- Passport records name the applicant and often family members — useful for identifying migration and family composition.

### Cemetery records
- **Held:** Madeira Regional Archive and parish records. Cemetery (civil/Catholic) burial registers overlap with church death registers.
- **Online:** Not specifically confirmed from tool results; FindAGrave and BillionGraves may have partial coverage.

### Emigration records
- Madeira had significant emigration to Hawaii 1878–1911 and Brazil throughout the 19th century. Resources include:
  - Portuguese Hawaiian Genealogy resources (yourislandroutes.com; digitalcollections.hawaii.gov — Portuguese Passenger Manifests, Hawaii 1843–1900).
  - Hamburg Passenger Lists 1850–1934 (some Portuguese emigrants traveled via Hamburg).
  - Immigrant Ships Transcribers Guild (immigrantships.net — passenger lists from Portuguese ports).

## Repository guide

### Online repositories
| Repository | Collections for this place | Access |
|---|---|---|
| FamilySearch | Portugal, Madeira, Catholic Church Records, 1044-1990 (coll. 4426199); Portugal Baptisms 1570-1910; Marriages 1670-1910; Deaths 1640-1910; Civil Records 1437-2023 | Free |
| Tombo.pt | tombo.pt/en/d/madeira — Madeira civil registration, church records, passports | Free |
| Ancestry | Portugal Select Baptisms, Marriages, Deaths (1570-1910); Madeira Passports 1872-1910 | Subscription |
| FindMyPast | Portugal Baptism/Marriage/Death Indexes 1570-1910 | Subscription |
| MyHeritage | Portugal Baptisms, Marriages, Deaths 1570-1910 | Subscription |
| Madeira Regional Archive (ABM) | abm.madeira.gov.pt — passports, civil registration search | Free (online search) |

### Physical repositories
| Repository | Holdings | Access method |
|---|---|---|
| Arquivo Regional da Madeira (ABM) | Original parish registers, civil registration, passports, notarial acts | In-person, Funchal; online catalog at biblioteca.abm.madeira.gov.pt |
| Arquivo Nacional Torre do Tombo (ANTT), Lisbon | National-level records; some Madeira content | In-person or via digitarq.arquivos.pt |
| Diocese of Funchal Archives | Diocesan records not yet digitized | Contact diocese |

## Records NOT online
- Portuguese national census records (1864, 1878, 1890, 1900) — held at ANTT and ABM, not systematically indexed online.
- Róis de Confessados (annual parishioner lists) — partial access via ANTT; not indexed on FamilySearch.
- Notarial records (escrituras, testamentos) — held physically at ABM and notarial archives.
- Some later civil registration volumes not yet fully digitized.

## Known record losses
No major record destruction events specifically confirmed from tool results for Funchal. Madeira was not significantly affected by military conflict in the 1860–1900 period. However, natural degradation and incomplete microfilming mean coverage gaps exist for some parishes and years.

## Research tips
- **Identify the correct parish first.** Funchal municipality contained multiple parishes (Santo António, Sé, São Pedro, São Gonçalo, Santa Maria Maior, etc.). Knowing the subject's parish dramatically narrows the search. Antonio Fernandes Lucas's parish is not confirmed in the tree — search the national Madeira collection (4426199) by name first, then drill into parish-specific volumes.
- **Name variations.** Portuguese names from this period often appear with variant spellings and without middle names in some records. "Fernandes" may appear abbreviated or in variant forms. "de Jesus" is a very common Marian surname/cognomen for women in 19th-century Madeira — expect many women named Antonia de Jesus.
- **Civil registration overlap.** After 1878, both parish and civil registers were kept; search both for completeness. FamilySearch collection 4426199 integrates both for Madeira.
- **Records are in Portuguese.** Some Latin in older registers. The standard format for a baptism record names the child, parents (including mother's full name), godparents, date and parish — exactly the evidence needed to identify the mother of a daughter named Maria.
- **Passport records supplement vital records.** For emigration-era families, passport applications (1872-1910) name family members and are worth searching.
- **Tombo.pt** (tombo.pt/en/d/madeira) is a direct portal to Madeira Catholic and civil records and is maintained by the Portuguese national archives — check it alongside FamilySearch.
- **ABM online catalog** (biblioteca.abm.madeira.gov.pt) allows searching by individual's name across Madeira records — use as a cross-check.

### Q_001: Did Antonio Fernandes Lucas (GK89-82B) marry Antonia de Jesus?
**Answer: Probably not** (ps_001, tier: probable, ev_002: consider_addressing — no blockers)

The two 1890 marriage records (Catholic 6BG7-FC2X and civil 6BG7-FC2X) establish GK89-82B's only documented marriage was to **Maria Joana de Jesus** on 8 Feb 1890. Three corroborating records (1859 marriage 6BG7-MQ3D, 1890 baptism 6NGD-3SZ7) consistently attribute all "Antonio Fernandes Lucas + Antonia de Jesus" associations to the **Manoel branch** (father=Manoel Fernandes Lucas), which is genealogically distinct from GK89-82B (father=José Fernandes Lucas). One open thread remains: h_001, the identity of the 1890 baptism father (I8) has not been independently confirmed by image review. This does not block the conclusion but prevents upgrading to "proved."

### Q_002: Did GK89-82B have a daughter named Maria who died young?
**Answer: Probably not** (ps_002, tier: probable, ev_005: looks_solid)

Five independent records across three record types were examined:

| Record | Type | Key exclusion marker |
|---|---|---|
| 6NG6-XHM2 (1886 baptism) | Catholic church | Grandfather = **Manuel** Fernandes Lucas (not José) |
| 6B2L-FKDG (1889 death) | Catholic church | Mother = **Antonia de Jesus** (not Maria Joana) |
| 6YPM-36RZ (1889 death) | **Civil registration** (independent) | Mother = **Antonia de Jesus** |
| 6NR2-ZMW7 (1892 baptism) | Catholic church | Mother's own parents = I8 + **Antonia de Jesus** (3rd generation) |
| 6BCT-KZMJ (1894 death) | Catholic church | Mother = **Antonia de Jesus** — post-marriage period covered |

All five candidates trace to the Manoel branch. The post-marriage window (1890–1910) is specifically addressed by records 4 and 5. No record with mother=Maria Joana de Jesus and daughter=Maria was found in any searched collection.
